chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Mutahhar who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan, the Master of the Barracks (peace be upon him), 'I have married four women, without asking for their names. Then I wanted to divorce one of them and marry another woman.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Look for a sign that is with one of them, and say: Bear witness that so-and-so, who has such and such a sign, is divorced. Then marry the other one when the waiting period expires.'
ai.seo_question: How to divorce a wife when her name is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in resolving the ambiguity of identity (gharar) in marital contracts, specifically when names are unknown. Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (AS) prescribes using a distinctive physical mark as a valid identifier for the specific wife, allowing for a precise declaration of divorce (talaq) without requiring the name. This ruling underscores the principle that clear identification is sufficient for legal validity, facilitating the subsequent remarriage after the completion of the waiting period (iddah).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Mutahhar who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Sahib Al-Askar<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I am married to four wives, not having even asked about their names. Then I wanted to divorce one of them and marry another woman’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Look at a sign which was with one of them, and you should be saying, ‘So and so woman who is with such and such a sign, she is divorced’. Then marry another one, when the waiting period expires’.
en.sarwar: 31. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja’far from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Mutahhar who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu al-Hassan Sahib al-‘Askar saying, ‘I have married four women and have not asked for their names. I want to divorce one of them and marry another woman. He (the Imam) wrote to me, ‘Look for a mark on any one of them and then say, ‘Bear witness that so and so who has such and such mark is divorced; then marry the other woman when waiting period is complete/”
